bull.b: The 20-year Rockdale lease adds substantial contracted revenue visibility and a potentially high-margin infrastructure stream beyond Bitcoin mining. Phased delivery and long-term extensions could support recurring cash generation, diversify the business, and improve the durability of Riot’s earnings mix.

Rapid engineering growth, improving margins, and a substantial data-center-focused backlog indicate useful internal capabilities rather than reliance solely on mining revenue. Increased manufacturing capacity may support timely project delivery, reduce lead-time exposure, and strengthen Riot’s position in infrastructure development.

Riot’s large deployed hash rate and low reported net power cost provide an operating advantage in a power-intensive industry. Efficient electricity management and meaningful production scale can support competitiveness through changing network conditions, while mining remains an established operating base.

bear.b: Severe losses across multiple earnings levels show that current operations are not converting strong revenue growth into sustainable profitability. This weak cost structure reduces internal funding capacity and leaves future earnings highly sensitive to operating conditions, project execution, and business mix.

Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow means Riot is consuming cash while pursuing a capital-intensive expansion. Continued burn can constrain flexibility, increase the need for financing or asset sales, and make the company more dependent on successful project ramp-up to fund long-term growth.

Using mined Bitcoin to fund data-center equity needs reduces the treasury asset base and links development capacity to ongoing asset sales. Alongside interim borrowing and large planned capital requirements, this creates execution and financing dependence before contracted projects begin contributing at scale.
